milestone.name: M1 + M2 — full PRD, single pass

decisions.question: Does this /spec pass shape only M1 ("Redirect works": FR-1,2,3,6,7, NFR-2,3,5), or both PRD milestones in one pass?
options: M1 only — defer M2 (FR-4,5,8, NFR-1,4,6) to a second /spec pass after M1 ships
M1 + M2 together — shape the full 14-requirement PRD now, preserving M1-before-M2 as build order rather than a scoping split
decisions.proposed_default: M1 + M2 together — shape the full 14-requirement PRD now, preserving M1-before-M2 as build order rather than a scoping split
decisions.chosen: M1 + M2 together — shape the full 14-requirement PRD now, preserving M1-before-M2 as build order rather than a scoping split
decisions.rationale: This run's explicit scope instruction is the entire PRD (M1 and M2, FR-1..FR-8, NFR-1..NFR-6) in one pass, not deferred. The PRD's own M1/M2 split is kept as epic build order (D5) rather than as a spec-scope cut, since a real dependency chain (auth → create → {redirect, list, delete}) already forces M1's epics to finish before M2's console epics can be verified end to end. Operator reviewed and confirmed this default on 2026-08-21.

decisions.question: How do the 14 requirements split into epics — vertical slices vs a layered Types→Config→Repository→Service→API→UI ladder?
options: 7 vertical-slice epics, one per user-observable capability: E1 Auth (FR-1,7,NFR-3), E2 Link Creation (FR-2,6,NFR-2), E3 Redirect (FR-3), E4 Console List (FR-4,NFR-1,NFR-4), E5 Delete (FR-5), E6 Health & Errors (FR-8,NFR-6), E7 Deploy & Environment (NFR-5)
Fewer, coarser epics (e.g. merge Auth+Creation, or merge Redirect+Delete since both act on an existing code)
A layered ladder (one epic per architectural layer, e.g. "Repository layer", "Service layer")
decisions.proposed_default: 7 vertical-slice epics, one per user-observable capability: E1 Auth (FR-1,7,NFR-3), E2 Link Creation (FR-2,6,NFR-2), E3 Redirect (FR-3), E4 Console List (FR-4,NFR-1,NFR-4), E5 Delete (FR-5), E6 Health & Errors (FR-8,NFR-6), E7 Deploy & Environment (NFR-5)
decisions.chosen: 7 vertical-slice epics, one per user-observable capability: E1 Auth (FR-1,7,NFR-3), E2 Link Creation (FR-2,6,NFR-2), E3 Redirect (FR-3), E4 Console List (FR-4,NFR-1,NFR-4), E5 Delete (FR-5), E6 Health & Errors (FR-8,NFR-6), E7 Deploy & Environment (NFR-5)
decisions.rationale: Each epic ships an independently demoable slice (tracer bullet), matching the shape guidance to avoid a layered ladder. FR-6 (SSRF/URL guard) stays inside E2 rather than becoming its own epic because the PRD enforces it only at creation time, literally on the host string (SG-10 forbids DNS/outbound resolution) — it is not a cross-cutting concern touched by other epics. Redirect (E3) and Delete (E5) stay separate epics rather than merging: they are independent user actions on an existing code with different observable outcomes (302 vs 204/404) and no shared code path beyond the link lookup. Operator reviewed and confirmed this default on 2026-08-21.

decisions.question: Which epic-to-epic dependencies are real (block story start) vs defensive (nice-to-sequence but not required)?
options: Real: E2→E1 (create requires a signed-in session), E3→E2 (redirect needs an existing link row), E4→{E1,E2} (list requires auth + existing links to list), E5→{E1,E2} (delete requires auth + an existing link). Defensive/none: E6 (health) and E7 (deploy) have no upstream epic dependency and can start immediately.
Treat all 7 epics as mutually independent and let story-level file ownership resolve conflicts at implement time
decisions.proposed_default: Real: E2→E1 (create requires a signed-in session), E3→E2 (redirect needs an existing link row), E4→{E1,E2} (list requires auth + existing links to list), E5→{E1,E2} (delete requires auth + an existing link). Defensive/none: E6 (health) and E7 (deploy) have no upstream epic dependency and can start immediately.
decisions.chosen: Real: E2→E1 (create requires a signed-in session), E3→E2 (redirect needs an existing link row), E4→{E1,E2} (list requires auth + existing links to list), E5→{E1,E2} (delete requires auth + an existing link). Defensive/none: E6 (health) and E7 (deploy) have no upstream epic dependency and can start immediately.
decisions.rationale: FR-2 is explicitly gated on being signed in; FR-3/4/5 all act on link rows that only exist after FR-2. Treating everything as independent would let the renderer schedule e.g. Delete stories before any link can exist, producing untestable acceptance criteria. Operator reviewed and confirmed this default on 2026-08-21.

decisions.question: Are any of the 7 epics or 14 requirements deferred out of this /spec pass (needs_breakdown) rather than rendered now?
options: No deferrals — render all 7 epics / 14 requirements this pass
Defer E4/E5/E6 (M2's console epics) to a later /spec pass
decisions.proposed_default: No deferrals — render all 7 epics / 14 requirements this pass
decisions.chosen: No deferrals — render all 7 epics / 14 requirements this pass
decisions.rationale: The run's explicit scope instruction says not to defer M2 to a later pass. All 14 requirements already have a clear epic home (D2) and a resolved dependency position (D3), so nothing here needs further breakdown before rendering. Operator reviewed and confirmed this default on 2026-08-21.

decisions.question: What build order do the 7 epics render in — does the PRD's M1-then-M2 sequencing carry through as epic order?
options: E7 (deploy/env scaffold) and E1 (auth) first and in parallel → E2 (creation) → E3, E4, E5 in parallel once E2 lands → E6 (health) any time after E7. This keeps M1's epics (E1,E2,E3,E7 plus NFR-2,3,5) ahead of M2's (E4,E5,E6 plus NFR-1,4,6) without a hard phase gate between them.
Strict two-phase gate: finish and fully verify every M1 epic before starting any M2 epic
decisions.proposed_default: E7 (deploy/env scaffold) and E1 (auth) first and in parallel → E2 (creation) → E3, E4, E5 in parallel once E2 lands → E6 (health) any time after E7. This keeps M1's epics (E1,E2,E3,E7 plus NFR-2,3,5) ahead of M2's (E4,E5,E6 plus NFR-1,4,6) without a hard phase gate between them.
decisions.chosen: E7 (deploy/env scaffold) and E1 (auth) first and in parallel → E2 (creation) → E3, E4, E5 in parallel once E2 lands → E6 (health) any time after E7. This keeps M1's epics (E1,E2,E3,E7 plus NFR-2,3,5) ahead of M2's (E4,E5,E6 plus NFR-1,4,6) without a hard phase gate between them.
decisions.rationale: The PRD's own milestone order (M1 done_when precedes M2 done_when) is honored as a build-order preference, not a scope gate — a hard gate would block E6 (health, independent of everything but E7) from starting early for no reason the dependency graph (D3) supports. Operator reviewed and confirmed this default on 2026-08-21.

decisions.question: NFR-1 ("create and list responses are p95 under 300ms at 100 links") spans two epics (E2 create, E4 list) — which epic owns it?
options: E4 (Console List) owns NFR-1, since verifying it needs both the create and list endpoints to exist, and E4 is built after E2 (D5)
Split NFR-1 into two separate per-epic performance requirements, one attached to E2 and one to E4
decisions.proposed_default: E4 (Console List) owns NFR-1, since verifying it needs both the create and list endpoints to exist, and E4 is built after E2 (D5)
decisions.chosen: E4 (Console List) owns NFR-1, since verifying it needs both the create and list endpoints to exist, and E4 is built after E2 (D5)
decisions.rationale: Splitting the requirement text would fork one acceptance criterion into two, which the BRD does not do (FRD-9 is a single requirement). Keeping single ownership on the later-built epic lets its acceptance test seed 100 links (via the already-built create endpoint) and then assert both endpoints' p95 in one place.
